paragraphs.title: Returning to One’s Heart and to the Lord

easy.question: What should a person do when the blessing and the curse come upon him?
answers: Call these things to mind
Leave the land
Choose only the blessing
easy.explanation: The verse says to call these things to mind—to think about and reflect on what has happened.

easy.question: Where were the Israelites scattered according to the verse?
answers: Into the wilderness
Among the nations
Into Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The Israelites are described as being among all the nations to which the Lord drove them.

easy.question: What are the people required to do in verse 2?
answers: Build a new house
Fight the nations
Return to the Lord and obey His voice
easy.explanation: The verse commands them to return to the Lord and obey His voice.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in these verses?
answers: The blessing and curse come, the people reflect, and then return to the Lord and obey Him
The people return to the Lord and then go into exile
The people obey the Lord and then the curse comes
medium.explanation: First the blessing and curse come upon them; then they call these things to mind; finally they return to the Lord and obey Him.

medium.question: What does “driven” mean in the phrase “among all the nations, whither the Lord thy God hath driven thee”?
answers: Blessed
Forced away or exiled
Taught
medium.explanation: The context of being among the nations indicates that they were forced away or sent into exile.

medium.question: Who is required to return to the Lord and obey His voice?
answers: Only the king
Only the elders
The person and his children
medium.explanation: The verse specifically includes “thou and thy children,” and says this must be done with all their heart and soul.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “the blessing and the curse”?
answers: The people may experience different results depending on their conduct
The blessing and the curse are the same thing
The verse speaks only about success
challenge.explanation: Mentioning both blessing and curse shows that the people may experience different consequences.

challenge.question: What does “return unto the Lord thy God” mean in this context?
answers: Move to another country
Return to serving and obeying the Lord
Return only to the place they left
challenge.explanation: The phrase that follows—obeying His voice—shows that returning to the Lord means a spiritual and practical return to loyalty and obedience.

challenge.question: What does “with all thine heart, and with all thy soul” emphasize?
answers: The command is only for children
Obedience should be partial and temporary
Returning to the Lord must be complete and wholehearted
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes full commitment, not merely an outward or partial response.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “the blessing and the curse”?
answers: The people may experience different results depending on their conduct
The blessing and the curse are the same thing
The verse speaks only about success
questions.explanation: Mentioning both blessing and curse shows that the people may experience different consequences.

questions.question: What does “return unto the Lord thy God” mean in this context?
answers: Move to another country
Return to serving and obeying the Lord
Return only to the place they left
questions.explanation: The phrase that follows—obeying His voice—shows that returning to the Lord means a spiritual and practical return to loyalty and obedience.

questions.question: What does “with all thine heart, and with all thy soul” emphasize?
answers: The command is only for children
Obedience should be partial and temporary
Returning to the Lord must be complete and wholehearted
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes full commitment, not merely an outward or partial response.

paragraphs.title: Gathering the Exiles and Restoring the People to the Land

easy.question: What will the Lord do for Israel according to these verses?
answers: Gather them from the nations
Leave them in exile
Prevent them from returning
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord will gather Israel from all the nations among which they were scattered.

easy.question: From where will the Lord gather Israel, even if they are very far away?
answers: Only from the land of Israel
From the outmost parts of heaven
From Egypt alone
easy.explanation: The verse emphasizes that even if they are at the outmost parts of heaven, the Lord will gather them from there.

easy.question: What will happen to Israel after the Lord brings them into the land?
answers: They will leave it immediately
They will remain few in number
They will possess the land and multiply
easy.explanation: The verse says they will possess the land, prosper, and multiply.

medium.question: What sequence is described in these verses?
answers: Gathering from the nations, bringing them into the land, possession, and blessing
Possession, exile, and then gathering
Multiplication, leaving the land, and then scattering
medium.explanation: First the Lord gathers the people, then brings them into the land, and finally prospers and multiplies them.

medium.question: What can we understand from the fact that the Lord will gather Israel even from the outmost parts of heaven?
answers: Distance will prevent their return
No place is too far for the gathering of the people
Only a few will be able to return
medium.explanation: The verse emphasizes that even extreme distance cannot prevent the Lord from gathering Israel.

medium.question: What does “driven out” mean in the phrase “If any of thine be driven out unto the outmost parts of heaven”?
answers: If you are established in your land
If you are happy where you are
If you are forced away and scattered
medium.explanation: The phrase describes people who have been forced away from their place and scattered over a great distance.

challenge.question: Why does the verse mention that even those at the outmost parts of heaven will be gathered?
answers: To emphasize that the return will include even the most distant
To teach that heaven is where Israel lives
To say that the land can be found only there
challenge.explanation: Mentioning the outmost parts of heaven reinforces that no distance or dispersion will prevent the gathering.

challenge.question: What does the repetition of “return” in verse 3 teach?
answers: The Lord repeatedly changes His mind
The Lord will restore and gather the people again
The people must remain scattered
challenge.explanation: The word appears in the context of restoring the people and gathering Israel from all the nations.

challenge.question: What special promise appears at the end of verse 5 concerning the fathers?
answers: The people will become exactly like their fathers
The people will not possess the land
The Lord will prosper and multiply the people more than their fathers
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the Lord will prosper Israel and multiply them more than their fathers.

questions.question: Why does the verse mention that even those at the outmost parts of heaven will be gathered?
answers: To emphasize that the return will include even the most distant
To teach that heaven is where Israel lives
To say that the land can be found only there
questions.explanation: Mentioning the outmost parts of heaven reinforces that no distance or dispersion will prevent the gathering.

questions.question: What does the repetition of “return” in verse 3 teach?
answers: The Lord repeatedly changes His mind
The Lord will restore and gather the people again
The people must remain scattered
questions.explanation: The word appears in the context of restoring the people and gathering Israel from all the nations.

questions.question: What special promise appears at the end of verse 5 concerning the fathers?
answers: The people will become exactly like their fathers
The people will not possess the land
The Lord will prosper and multiply the people more than their fathers
questions.explanation: The verse says that the Lord will prosper Israel and multiply them more than their fathers.

paragraphs.title: Circumcision of the Heart and the Blessing of Return

easy.question: What will the Lord do to the hearts of Israel and their descendants?
answers: He will circumcise their hearts
He will make them kings
He will take the land from them
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord will circumcise the hearts of the people and their descendants.

easy.question: Upon whom will the Lord place the curses?
answers: Upon Israel
Upon the enemies and haters who persecuted Israel
Upon Israel’s fathers
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord will place all the curses upon Israel’s enemies and those who hate them.

easy.question: What must Israel do after returning and obeying the Lord’s voice?
answers: Build a new city
Go to war
Keep all His commandments
easy.explanation: Verse 8 says that they will obey the Lord’s voice and do all His commandments.

medium.question: What does “rejoice” mean in “the Lord will again rejoice over thee for good”?
answers: Be glad
Become angry
Forget
medium.explanation: To rejoice means to be glad; the context says that the Lord will be glad to prosper Israel.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in these verses?
answers: Israel obeys the Lord and keeps His commandments, and then receives blessing
Israel receives prosperity and then begins pursuing its enemies
The enemies keep the commandments and then Israel returns to the Lord
medium.explanation: First Israel returns to the Lord and obeys Him; afterward the verses describe prosperity and blessing.

medium.question: Why will the Lord prosper Israel and the work of their hands?
answers: Because Israel will simply become numerous
Because Israel will return to the Lord with all its heart and soul
Because their enemies will help them
medium.explanation: Verse 10 connects prosperity with keeping the commandments and returning to the Lord wholeheartedly.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “thine heart, and the heart of thy seed”?
answers: The spiritual change is only for leaders
The change is intended for both the present generation and its descendants
The change will happen only after a war
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly mentions both the person’s heart and the heart of his descendants.

challenge.question: What is the connection between “that thou mayest live” and loving the Lord with all one’s heart and soul?
answers: Love for the Lord is presented as a path to life
Love for the Lord replaces keeping the commandments
Love for the Lord is only for defeating enemies
challenge.explanation: The verse mentions wholehearted love for the Lord and immediately gives its purpose: “that thou mayest live.”

challenge.question: What condition is repeated in verses 6–10 as a condition for the promised good?
answers: Separation from all the nations
Returning to the Lord and obeying His voice
Gathering great wealth
challenge.explanation: Returning to the Lord and obeying His voice recur in these verses and are connected with keeping His commandments and receiving good.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “thine heart, and the heart of thy seed”?
answers: The spiritual change is only for leaders
The change is intended for both the present generation and its descendants
The change will happen only after a war
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly mentions both the person’s heart and the heart of his descendants.

questions.question: What is the connection between “that thou mayest live” and loving the Lord with all one’s heart and soul?
answers: Love for the Lord is presented as a path to life
Love for the Lord replaces keeping the commandments
Love for the Lord is only for defeating enemies
questions.explanation: The verse mentions wholehearted love for the Lord and immediately gives its purpose: “that thou mayest live.”

questions.question: What condition is repeated in verses 6–10 as a condition for the promised good?
answers: Separation from all the nations
Returning to the Lord and obeying His voice
Gathering great wealth
questions.explanation: Returning to the Lord and obeying His voice recur in these verses and are connected with keeping His commandments and receiving good.

paragraphs.title: The Commandment Is Near and Accessible

easy.question: What is said about the commandment in verse 11?
answers: It is not too difficult or beyond reach
It was given only to angels
It is forbidden to human beings
easy.explanation: The verse says that the commandment is not hidden from the people and is not far away.

easy.question: Which two places are mentioned as places where the commandment is not found?
answers: The wilderness and the mountain
Heaven and beyond the sea
The land and the house
easy.explanation: Verses 12–13 say that the commandment is not in heaven and is not beyond the sea.

easy.question: Where is the word found according to verse 14?
answers: Only in heaven
Only beyond the sea
In the person’s mouth and heart
easy.explanation: The verse says that the word is very near, in the person’s mouth and heart, so that he may do it.

medium.question: Why is there no need to go up to heaven or cross the sea to keep the commandment?
answers: Because the commandment is near and can be carried out
Because the sea and heaven do not exist
Because only priests may keep it
medium.explanation: The verses explain that no distant journey is necessary because the word is near and can be obeyed.

medium.question: What is the sequence of ideas in these verses?
answers: They first describe action and then distance
They first rule out heaven, then beyond the sea, and finally say that the word is near
They first discuss the sea, then the heart, and finally heaven
medium.explanation: The verses move from heaven, to beyond the sea, and then conclude that the word is near the person.

medium.question: What does “hidden” mean in the phrase “it is not hidden from thee”?
answers: It does not belong to you
It is found only in a secret place
It is not too difficult or beyond your understanding
medium.explanation: In context, saying that the commandment is not hidden means that it is not too difficult or inaccessible to understand.

challenge.question: What excuse may a person not make according to these verses?
answers: That the commandment is too far away to know or obey
That the commandment was given today
That the commandment concerns the heart and mouth
challenge.explanation: The verses reject the claim that the commandment is inaccessible because it is in heaven or beyond the sea.

challenge.question: What does the repeated question “Who shall go up?” or “Who shall go over?” teach?
answers: A messenger must be sent to heaven and across the sea
Imagining an impossible journey is an excuse; no such journey is required
Only one person can know the commandment
challenge.explanation: The questions describe an imagined need to bring the commandment from far away, but the verses immediately show that this is unnecessary.

challenge.question: What is the full meaning of “the word is very nigh unto thee”?
answers: It is located only near the person’s home
A person only has to speak about the commandment
The commandment is accessible in thought, speech, and action
challenge.explanation: The verse says it is in the mouth and heart and adds “that thou mayest do it,” so it can be understood, spoken, and practiced.

questions.question: What excuse may a person not make according to these verses?
answers: That the commandment is too far away to know or obey
That the commandment was given today
That the commandment concerns the heart and mouth
questions.explanation: The verses reject the claim that the commandment is inaccessible because it is in heaven or beyond the sea.

questions.question: What does the repeated question “Who shall go up?” or “Who shall go over?” teach?
answers: A messenger must be sent to heaven and across the sea
Imagining an impossible journey is an excuse; no such journey is required
Only one person can know the commandment
questions.explanation: The questions describe an imagined need to bring the commandment from far away, but the verses immediately show that this is unnecessary.

questions.question: What is the full meaning of “the word is very nigh unto thee”?
answers: It is located only near the person’s home
A person only has to speak about the commandment
The commandment is accessible in thought, speech, and action
questions.explanation: The verse says it is in the mouth and heart and adds “that thou mayest do it,” so it can be understood, spoken, and practiced.

paragraphs.title: Choosing Between Life and Good and Between Death and Evil

easy.question: What did Moses set before the people?
answers: Life and good, and death and evil
The wilderness and the sea
The king and the priest
easy.explanation: The verse says, “I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil.”

easy.question: What does the Lord command Israel to do?
answers: Build new cities
Love the Lord, walk in His ways, and keep His commandments
Go to war immediately
easy.explanation: The verse commands Israel to love the Lord, walk in His ways, and keep His commandments, statutes, and judgments.

easy.question: What will happen if the people keep the Lord’s words?
answers: They will return to Egypt
They will remain in the wilderness
They will live, multiply, and be blessed in the land
easy.explanation: The verse promises, “thou mayest live and multiply,” and that the Lord will bless them in the land.

medium.question: What connection does the verse present between keeping the Lord’s commandments and the people’s future?
answers: Keeping the commandments leads to life, multiplication, and blessing in the land
Keeping the commandments causes the people to leave the land
Keeping the commandments prevents the people from multiplying
medium.explanation: After commanding love and obedience, the verse describes life, multiplication, and blessing in the land.

medium.question: What does “to possess it” mean in “the land whither thou goest to possess it”?
answers: To leave it
To receive and hold it as an inheritance
To hide in it
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the people are going to receive the land and hold it as their inheritance.

medium.question: What is the central sequence in the verse?
answers: Blessing in the land, then commandment, and finally choice
Leaving the land, then war, and finally rest
Commanding love and obedience, followed by life, multiplication, and blessing in the land
medium.explanation: The command to love and obey the Lord comes first, followed by the result: life, multiplication, and blessing in the land.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from setting “life and good” against “death and evil”?
answers: The people face a choice with different consequences
All the choices lead to the same result
The verse concerns only physical conditions, not conduct
challenge.explanation: The contrast between life and good and death and evil emphasizes that the people’s choices have different consequences.

challenge.question: Why are love for the Lord, walking in His ways, and keeping His commandments mentioned together?
answers: To describe three different festivals
To show that love for the Lord is expressed through conduct and obedience
To distinguish the Lord from the land
challenge.explanation: The verse connects love, walking in the right way, and keeping the commandments, showing that love is also a practical way of life.

challenge.question: What detail can be understood from “the land whither thou goest to possess it”?
answers: The Israelites have already left the land
The land is unrelated to the Lord’s blessing
The Israelites are still on their way to the land and will receive it as an inheritance
challenge.explanation: “Whither thou goest” shows that the people are still approaching the land, while “to possess it” shows that they will receive it as an inheritance.

questions.question: What can be inferred from setting “life and good” against “death and evil”?
answers: The people face a choice with different consequences
All the choices lead to the same result
The verse concerns only physical conditions, not conduct
questions.explanation: The contrast between life and good and death and evil emphasizes that the people’s choices have different consequences.

questions.question: Why are love for the Lord, walking in His ways, and keeping His commandments mentioned together?
answers: To describe three different festivals
To show that love for the Lord is expressed through conduct and obedience
To distinguish the Lord from the land
questions.explanation: The verse connects love, walking in the right way, and keeping the commandments, showing that love is also a practical way of life.

questions.question: What detail can be understood from “the land whither thou goest to possess it”?
answers: The Israelites have already left the land
The land is unrelated to the Lord’s blessing
The Israelites are still on their way to the land and will receive it as an inheritance
questions.explanation: “Whither thou goest” shows that the people are still approaching the land, while “to possess it” shows that they will receive it as an inheritance.

paragraphs.title: Warning Against Turning to Other Gods

easy.question: What will the Israelites do if their hearts turn away and they do not obey?
answers: Worship other gods
Build the tabernacle
Return to Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse says that they will be drawn away, worship other gods, and serve them.

easy.question: What punishment is described for those who do not obey and worship other gods?
answers: They will become wealthy
They will perish and not live long in the land
They will receive another land
easy.explanation: The verse warns, “ye shall surely perish,” and says they will not prolong their days in the land.

easy.question: Which river are they about to cross to enter the land?
answers: The Nile
The Euphrates
The Jordan
easy.explanation: The verse refers to crossing the Jordan to enter and possess the land.

medium.question: According to the verses, what leads to worshiping other gods?
answers: The heart turning away and refusing to obey
Crossing the Jordan
Possessing the land
medium.explanation: First the heart turns away and the person refuses to listen; then he is drawn away to worship other gods.

medium.question: What does “turn away” mean in “if thine heart turn away”?
answers: Fall asleep
Turn in another direction and depart
Become joyful
medium.explanation: The context of disobedience and idolatry shows that the heart turns aside and departs from the right path.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in these verses?
answers: Perishing, crossing the Jordan, and then turning to other gods
Worshiping other gods, possessing the land, and then obeying
The heart turns away and refuses to obey, the people worship other gods, and then they perish
medium.explanation: The verses first describe turning away and refusing to listen, then idolatry, and finally destruction and shortened days in the land.

challenge.question: What does “ye shall surely perish” teach about the severity of the punishment?
answers: The destruction is certain and serious
The destruction will be temporary only
The destruction applies only to possessions
challenge.explanation: The emphatic wording stresses both the certainty and seriousness of the destruction.

challenge.question: What connection do the verses make between worshiping other gods and remaining in the land?
answers: Idolatry will lengthen their stay in the land
Idolatry will cause them not to live long in the land
There is no connection between them
challenge.explanation: The verse connects turning away and idolatry with the warning that they will not prolong their days in the land.

challenge.question: What can be understood from “I denounce unto you this day” in the context of crossing the Jordan?
answers: The warning was given after Israel lost the land
The warning was given while Israel was about to enter the land
The warning was given to a generation that had already lived in the land for many years
challenge.explanation: The verse describes the land they are crossing the Jordan to possess, so the warning is given before their entry.

questions.question: What does “ye shall surely perish” teach about the severity of the punishment?
answers: The destruction is certain and serious
The destruction will be temporary only
The destruction applies only to possessions
questions.explanation: The emphatic wording stresses both the certainty and seriousness of the destruction.

questions.question: What connection do the verses make between worshiping other gods and remaining in the land?
answers: Idolatry will lengthen their stay in the land
Idolatry will cause them not to live long in the land
There is no connection between them
questions.explanation: The verse connects turning away and idolatry with the warning that they will not prolong their days in the land.

questions.question: What can be understood from “I denounce unto you this day” in the context of crossing the Jordan?
answers: The warning was given after Israel lost the land
The warning was given while Israel was about to enter the land
The warning was given to a generation that had already lived in the land for many years
questions.explanation: The verse describes the land they are crossing the Jordan to possess, so the warning is given before their entry.

paragraphs.title: Heaven and Earth Bear Witness: Choose Life

easy.question: Which two options did Moses set before the people?
answers: Life and death
Wealth and poverty
War and peace
easy.explanation: The verse says, “I have set before you life and death.”

easy.question: What does Moses command the people to choose?
answers: The curse
Life
Death
easy.explanation: Moses explicitly commands them, “therefore choose life.”

easy.question: For whose benefit will choosing life be?
answers: For Moses alone
For the fathers alone
For the person and his descendants
easy.explanation: The verse says, “that both thou and thy seed may live.”

medium.question: What is promised as a result of choosing life?
answers: The people will no longer need to obey the Lord
The person and his descendants will live
The people will immediately receive wealth
medium.explanation: The reason given for choosing life is the result: “that both thou and thy seed may live.”

medium.question: What does “cleave unto him” mean in “that thou mayest cleave unto him”?
answers: Turn away from Him
Argue with Him
Remain closely attached and loyal to Him
medium.explanation: The phrase appears alongside loving and obeying the Lord, so it means remaining closely connected and faithful to Him.

medium.question: What sequence does the verse give concerning the relationship with the Lord?
answers: Love Him, obey His voice, and cleave to Him
Cleave to Him, ignore Him, and then love Him
Obey His voice, leave Him, and then choose the curse
medium.explanation: The verse lists three actions in sequence: love the Lord, obey His voice, and cleave to Him.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “he is thy life, and the length of thy days”?
answers: The land is the only source of life
Life depends only on the person himself
The Lord is the source of life and grants long life
challenge.explanation: The verse calls the Lord “thy life” and says He is the length of one’s days, presenting Him as the source of life and existence.

challenge.question: Why are heaven and earth mentioned at the beginning of Moses’ words?
answers: To serve as witnesses to the declaration and the choice set before the people
To describe where Moses lived
To say that the people should choose only the land
challenge.explanation: The phrase “I call heaven and earth to record this day” presents them as witnesses to the statement and the choice.

challenge.question: What connection is presented between loving the Lord and dwelling in the land?
answers: Loving the Lord causes the people to leave the land
Loving the Lord, obeying Him, and cleaving to Him are connected with living in the land promised to the fathers
Dwelling in the land is completely unrelated to a person’s conduct
challenge.explanation: The verse connects love and loyalty to the Lord with long life and dwelling in the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “he is thy life, and the length of thy days”?
answers: The land is the only source of life
Life depends only on the person himself
The Lord is the source of life and grants long life
questions.explanation: The verse calls the Lord “thy life” and says He is the length of one’s days, presenting Him as the source of life and existence.

questions.question: Why are heaven and earth mentioned at the beginning of Moses’ words?
answers: To serve as witnesses to the declaration and the choice set before the people
To describe where Moses lived
To say that the people should choose only the land
questions.explanation: The phrase “I call heaven and earth to record this day” presents them as witnesses to the statement and the choice.

questions.question: What connection is presented between loving the Lord and dwelling in the land?
answers: Loving the Lord causes the people to leave the land
Loving the Lord, obeying Him, and cleaving to Him are connected with living in the land promised to the fathers
Dwelling in the land is completely unrelated to a person’s conduct
questions.explanation: The verse connects love and loyalty to the Lord with long life and dwelling in the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
